authorization_policy_operation_type.description: Provide the operation type of the authorization policy. Allowed values: add authorization policy, modify authorization policy, delete authorization policy, query authorization policy.
authorization_policy_operation_type.x-a2at-value-constraint: Allowed values: add authorization policy, modify authorization policy, delete authorization policy, query authorization policy. When the input contains an allowed value itself or its abbreviation (e.g., "add", "modify", "delete", "query"), map it directly to the corresponding allowed value. Recognized synonym pairs are limited to: create/new/append→add authorization policy, update/edit/change to/adjust to→modify authorization policy, remove/take away/clear→delete authorization policy, view/retrieve/search/find/look up→query authorization policy. Any other verbs not in this list (e.g., export, import, sync, copy, migrate, suspend, approve, archive, download, backup) are out of range and must not be mapped to any allowed value.

network_operation_authorization_policy_l.description: Provide the network operation authorization policy list, multiple entries separated by semicolons.
examples: service complaint diagnosis/service recovery/tunnel optimization/2026-06-01~2030-06-18; carrier scheduling/service recovery/carrier scheduling/permanently valid
network_operation_authorization_policy_l.x-a2at-value-constraint: List text form. Each item contains: policy identifier (UUID unique identifier), business scenario (e.g. service complaint diagnosis), handling type (e.g. service recovery), operation name (e.g. tunnel optimization), validity period. The validity period is a date range (common date notations are acceptable, timestamps not required, date notations may differ across entries within the same list, date values must be real and valid) or "permanently valid"; both are valid. add authorization policy: required; each entry must contain business scenario, handling type, operation name, and validity period — four fields in total, no policy identifier needed; the validity period must be a complete range or "permanently valid"; a single date alone is treated as an incomplete range; field values must be meaningful business content, and meaningless characters (e.g., xxx, ###) constitute a format error. modify authorization policy: the entry format is "policy identifier/new validity period" (e.g., 7d8c7b00-3c8c-4f8e-9b1e-9b17b6a3e5c3/2026-06-01~2030-06-18, before '/' is the policy identifier, after '/' is the new validity period); an entry may also contain only the new validity period (treated as batch modification, equally valid), or be a combination of a policy identifier and a natural-language modification description (e.g., "7d8c7b00-3c8c-4f8e-9b1e-9b17b6a3e5c3, change the validity period to 2026-06-01~2030-06-18"), or a natural-language modification description alone (e.g., "change the validity period to 2026-01-01~2028-12-31", "change the validity period to permanently valid", equally valid); the new validity period may be a date range, a single date, or "permanently valid"; only the validity period can be modified, and modification intents on other fields are invalid; an entry with only a policy identifier and no new validity period or modification description is an invalid modification request. delete authorization policy: the entry is a policy identifier; a condition-style description is also valid — filter descriptions such as "handling type is service recovery" or "validity period expired", or a bare condition field value (e.g., "service complaint diagnosis", treated as deleting by filter on that business scenario) — are all equally valid. query authorization policy: optional; not providing this parameter is fully valid; query conditions may be one or more arbitrary values of business scenario, handling type, or operation name (filter conditions in the input, e.g., "service complaint diagnosis" in "query the network operation authorization policies of service complaint diagnosis", belong to query conditions and should be the value of this parameter; extract any value as-is at the extraction stage, and validity is decided by the validation stage), no complete entry format required. A query condition value is valid by default; it is treated as nonexistent only when the value itself declares nonexistence (e.g., contains self-declared-nonexistent wording such as "nonexistent" — for example "nonexistent scenario XYZ") or is meaningless characters. When an explicit policy identifier appears but is not in UUID format, the policy cannot be located.
